title: opto-sync ingest envelope
description: A JSON file/blob that can be ingested into opto-sync and synchronized to every store (IndexedDB, SQLite, Postgres, Supabase). One envelope carries one or more records; each record's payload must carry the timestamp fields that drive CRDT resolution. This document is the single cross-language source of truth: every TypeScript, Rust, Dart, Gleam, Go, and Java validator must accept/reject exactly the fixture corpus in fixtures/.

source.description: Free-form provenance label (device id, export job, ...). Length is measured in Unicode code points, as required by JSON Schema.

recordId.description: Record identity. Length is measured in Unicode code points.

payload.description: The jsonb document. updatedAt is required for upserts so last-write-wins is never decided by ingest order; createdAt/syncedAt are optional (createdAt is deliberately NOT a default FWW key). Objects nested in keyed arrays carry their own timestamps.

keyedElement.description: Contract for object elements inside MERGE_BY_KEY arrays: an identity plus optional per-element timestamps. Identity values must be unique within one array (duplicate identities are documented out-of-contract in the merge core).

identity.description: MERGE_BY_KEY identity: a non-empty string or an integer (int 42 matches "42" in the core).

timestamp.description: One timestamp FORMAT per key across all replicas (mixing formats compares lexicographically and is not chronologically meaningful). Accepted: native HLC string as emitted by the clients' formatHlc, plain fixed-width ISO-8601 UTC (optionally with suffixes), a non-negative JSON integer within the interoperable IEEE-754 safe range, or a pure-digit string. Larger epoch values must use the digit-string form so JavaScript, Dart web, Go, Java, Rust, and BEAM preserve the exact value.

oneOf.description: Native HLC as emitted by formatHlc/formatHlc()/format_hlc in the TypeScript, Dart, and Rust clients: 13-digit millis, 4-hex counter, nodeId. Fixed width is load-bearing — it makes lexicographic order equal chronological order. nodeId cannot contain '-' because '-' delimits the wire format (the clock constructor rejects it), which is what keeps this pattern unambiguous.
Fixed-width ISO-8601 UTC, optionally with counter/node suffixes appended after the Z.
